title: JIJ Launches SQOA Solver in IBM Quantum Functions Catalog to Tackle Combinatorial Optimization Beyond Qubit Counts - Quantum Computing Report
gist: JIJ Inc. put its SQOA Solver in the IBM Quantum Functions Catalog for Premium, Flex and On-Prem users. Its (3,1) QRAC relaxation packs up to three binary variables per qubit, and it replaces QAOA-style variational loops with single-pass quantum sampling plus classical subspace diagonalization. On IBM Heron r2 it solved a 384-node MaxCut on 129 qubits at a 98.5% approximation ratio and a 200-node MIS on 67 qubits at a 100% approximation ratio.

themes.theme: Fewer qubits than variables via QRAC

insights.claim: JIJ Inc.'s SQOA Solver, now in the IBM Quantum Functions Catalog for IBM Quantum Premium, Flex, and On-Prem Plan users, solves combinatorial optimization problems with more decision variables than available physical qubits.
insights.so_what: IBM's Functions Catalog is becoming a distribution channel for third-party quantum software; every listing expands what paying IBM Quantum customers can run.
insights.locator: Tokyo-based optimization software developer JIJ Inc.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem

insights.claim: SQOA Solver uses a (3,1) Quantum Random Access Code (QRAC) relaxation that maps up to three binary variables per physical qubit using Pauli X, Y, and Z operators.
insights.so_what: Up to three times the variable capacity per qubit effectively multiplies usable problem size on current hardware without waiting for larger QPUs.
insights.quote: Maps up to three binary variables per physical qubit using Pauli X, Y, and Z operators.

insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem

insights.claim: Variational algorithms like QAOA typically need one physical qubit per binary variable and repeated quantum-classical optimization loops that accumulate hardware noise as circuit depth grows. SQOA Solver avoids both by packing non-interacting variables onto shared qubits and using the QPU only to sample bitstrings from a relaxed Hamiltonian.
insights.so_what: This is part of a broader industry shift from variational loops to sample-then-classically-diagonalize (SQD-style) methods; QAOA-centric roadmaps look increasingly dated.

insights.claim: In SQOA Solver, state-preparation parameters are computed classically, and classical nodes project the relaxed Hamiltonian onto the subspace spanned by the sampled bitstrings, diagonalize it, and apply rounding and local search to recover feasible assignments.
insights.so_what: The heavy lifting is classical, which keeps QPU time short (12.0 s in the MaxCut benchmark) but also means classical compute costs and comparisons to classical heuristics matter.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem

insights.claim: On IBM Heron r2, SQOA Solver solved a 384-node 3-regular MaxCut instance on 129 qubits at a 98.5% approximation ratio with 12.0 seconds of QPU time, and a 200-node QOBLIB Maximum Independent Set instance on 67 qubits at a 100% approximation ratio.
insights.so_what: Roughly 3x variable compression with near-optimal results on standard benchmarks is an important proof point, though these instance sizes remain easy for classical solvers.
insights.quote: Solved 384-node MaxCut on 129 qubits (98.5% AR, 12.0 s QPU) and 200-node MIS on 67 qubits (100% AR).
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem

insights.claim: SQOA Solver ingests QUBO dictionaries, qiskit-addon-opt-mapper models, and Open Mathematical Programming eXchange (OMMX) instances compiled through JIJ's JijModeling 2, so enterprise teams can move the same model between classical solvers and IBM Quantum hardware.
insights.so_what: Solver-agnostic modeling lowers switching costs for enterprises and positions JIJ's modeling layer as sticky infrastructure regardless of which backend wins.

insights.claim: SQOA Solver offers Small (up to 50 variables), Medium (up to 100 variables), and Large (up to 48 vCPU / 768 GB RAM) compute profiles.
insights.so_what: Tiered sizing suggests usage-based monetization inside IBM's catalog, but current tiers still cover small problem sizes.
